meta.title: AI futures, 2026 — forecasting, control, and alignment sources
meta.provenance: Ranked list supplied to The Model Stack on 2026-09-27; rank, name, geography, AI-2027 fit score and reason reproduced verbatim (tracking parameters removed). Canonical URL, verification status and description come from loading each source on 2026-09-27; kind and chapter anchors are the atlas’s classification.

entries.name: AI 2027
entries.description: Month-by-month scenario of AI development up to superhuman AI, written for predictive accuracy rather than advocacy and branching into a race ending and a slowdown ending. Supplementary forecasts on compute, timelines, takeoff, AI goals, and security give the quantitative inputs behind it.

entries.name: AI Futures Project
entries.description: Nonprofit forecasting group behind AI 2027 and AI 2040; its site plots the team’s probability distributions for when AI fully automates software engineering and links its timelines-and-takeoff model.

verification.note: ai-futures.org, the address given on ai-2027.com/about, redirects (HTTP 307) to this domain.

entries.name: AI 2040
entries.description: Follow-on scenario to AI 2027 that sets out a recommended path through superintelligence (“Plan A”: a verified slowdown under an international agreement to avoid a race) against four alternatives: fight China, burn the lead, race to ASI, and shut it all down.

entries.name: AI Futures Model
entries.description: Interactive timelines-and-takeoff model whose output is the trajectory of AI’s ability to automate AI software R&D, staged by milestones such as the Automated Coder and the Superhuman AI Researcher. Forecasts come from repeated simulation over the team’s parameter distributions, then adjusted for out-of-model considerations.

entries.name: Situational Awareness
entries.description: June 2024 essay series arguing, by counting orders of magnitude of compute and algorithmic gains, that AGI by 2027 is plausible and that automated AI research could compress a decade of algorithmic progress into a year or less. Later chapters cover trillion-dollar compute clusters, lab security, superalignment, and US–China competition.

verification.note: The site names no publishing organisation or location; geography as supplied.

entries.name: AI Futures Project Forecasts
entries.description: Forecast pages of the AI Futures Project: dated, per-forecaster percentile dates for milestones such as the Automated Coder, produced by simulating the AI Futures Model over each forecaster’s parameter distributions.

verification.note: Listed with the same address as #2. The organisation’s model site links its forecasts here (“You can find our forecasts here”); the page renders client-side, so its content was confirmed from that link and from search results on the domain.

entries.name: Forecasting Research Institute
entries.description: Develops forecasting methods for high-stakes decisions and applies them to AI: the Longitudinal Expert AI Panel (LEAP) tracks expert forecasts of AI’s trajectory, ForecastBench scores the forecasting accuracy of AI systems, and it ran the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament.

entries.name: FRI Research
entries.description: Index of the institute’s projects and working papers, including LEAP (a three-year panel of computer scientists, industry professionals, policy researchers, and economists forecasting AI’s trajectory), the Automated AI Risk Outlook (catastrophic-risk probabilities forecast by an ensemble of frontier models), and a review of how accurate past AI-progress forecasts have been.

verification.note: ForecastBench is linked from the homepage (forecastbench.org), not from this index.

entries.name: Epoch AI
entries.reason: Capability, compute and AI trajectory measurement
entries.description: Research institute measuring the trends behind AI’s trajectory: it maintains the Epoch Capabilities Index, a database of more than 3,200 machine-learning models, a benchmarking hub, the FrontierMath benchmark, and an open database of large AI data centres, and publishes analyses of scaling, software progress, and capabilities.

entries.name: METR
entries.description: Nonprofit that evaluates whether and when frontier AI systems could cause catastrophic harm. Its central measurement is the task-completion time horizon — the length of task, in human-expert time, that an agent completes at a given success rate — which it reports has grown exponentially over the past six years.

verification.note: Formerly ARC Evals.

entries.name: METR Time Horizons
entries.description: Periodically updated 50% and 80% time horizons of public frontier models, estimated from agent performance on more than a hundred software tasks with known human-expert durations; METR reports that an exponential trend fits better than linear or hyperbolic ones.

verification.note: The listed address is METR’s former ARC Evals domain; it still serves a copy, but the page declares metr.org/time-horizons/ canonical and metr.org links it.

entries.name: Future of Life Institute — Futures
entries.description: Future of Life Institute programme on steering transformative technology toward beneficial outcomes; its Tomorrow’s AI project publishes 13 interactive, research-backed scenarios of how advanced AI could reshape the world, alongside work on AI and the distribution of power.

verification.note: The listed address is FLI’s homepage; the Futures programme is at /our-work/futures/, and the scenarios themselves are hosted at tomorrows-ai.org.

entries.name: MIT FutureTech
entries.description: MIT research group studying the foundations of progress in computing and AI — algorithmic progress, hardware trends, and which tasks are cost-effective to automate with AI — and maintaining the AI Risk Repository, a database and taxonomy of AI risks.

verification.note: The site presents trend measurement and its economic effects rather than forecasting.

entries.name: MIT FutureTech Research
entries.description: Research pillars (Processor Database, Computer Progress, Algorithm Wiki, AI Risk) and publications on algorithmic progress in language models, datacenter-GPU progress, which tasks are cost-effective to automate, and a quantitative task-based theory of AI and scale.

entries.name: CNAS — Superpowers and AGI
entries.org: Center for a New American Security (CNAS)
entries.description: August 2026 report that assumes AGI emerges rather than predicting when, and traces five mechanisms by which it could shift US–China power — economic growth, the information environment, military capability, misalignment or loss of control, and downstream political effects — through phases from both states pursuing AGI to one or both possessing it.

entries.name: BIGAI — Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence
entries.org: Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence (BIGAI)
entries.description: Nonprofit general-AI institute supported by the Beijing municipal government and the Ministry of Science and Technology with Peking and Tsinghua universities; it reports work on general agents (TongAgents), the TongSIM physical-simulation training environment, 3D scene data for embodied agents, and robot motion control.

entries.name: BIGAI Research
entries.org: Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence (BIGAI)
entries.description: Paper index of the institute (2021–2026), tagged by vision, language, machine learning, multi-agent systems, cognition and reasoning, simulation and interaction, and robotics, with recent work on safety alignment, agent-based simulation of moral evolution, and backdoor attacks on multi-agent systems.

verification.note: A publication index rather than a blog; “world models” is not among its topic tags.

entries.name: Shanghai AI Laboratory
entries.reason: Explicit open, controllable, trustworthy AGI vision
entries.description: Research laboratory whose stated vision is open, controllable, trustworthy AGI; it releases the Intern (书生) model family — including the Intern-S1 scientific multimodal model and the Intern-SafeWork safety stack — and the OpenCompass evaluation system.

entries.name: Moonshot AI
entries.description: Developer of the Kimi models and agents (Kimi Agent, Agent Swarm, Kimi Code), with a stated research goal of AGI; it describes its current model, Kimi K3, as natively multimodal with 2.8T parameters and a 1M-token context for long-horizon coding and reasoning.

entries.name: Kimi Research
entries.description: Moonshot AI’s research blog: technical write-ups of the Kimi K2, K2 Thinking, K2.5, K2.6, and K3 releases, the Agent Swarm system, and the WorldVQA and PerceptionBench benchmarks.

verification.note: The listed kimi.com address still loads, but the page declares kimi.ai/blog/ canonical and Moonshot AI’s homepage links it.

entries.name: DeepSeek Research & News
entries.description: DeepSeek’s release and research index: model releases (DeepSeek-V3.2 with DeepSeek Sparse Attention, the open V4 preview with 1M-token context, V4.1-Flash) and technical reports on long-context efficiency, conditional memory (Engram), manifold-constrained hyper-connections, and self-verifiable mathematical reasoning.

verification.note: The AGI orientation the supplier cites is a one-line mission statement; the page carries no forecasting or safety content.

entries.name: BAAI / Beijing Academy of AI
entries.reason: Frontier models, safety, evaluation, world models
entries.description: Beijing research institute releasing open model families (the WuJie line including the Emu3 multimodal world model, RoboBrain embodied models, BGE embeddings), the FlagOpen open-source stack, and the FlagEval evaluation system, with an AI-safety programme tied to the Beijing International Dialogue on AI Safety.

entries.name: FlagEval
entries.description: BAAI’s model-evaluation platform: leaderboards, an arena, and debate-format evaluations of open and closed models across language, multimodal, vision, and audio tasks, using unified evaluation environments and frequently refreshed, non-public test sets to limit leakage.

entries.name: FlagSafe
entries.description: BAAI’s large-model safety platform: red-team evaluation (including deception detection and VLA-Arena for embodied AI), defences (Align Anything, agent protection), and interpretability tools, organised around red lines from the Beijing International Consensus on AI Safety — autonomous replication or self-improvement, power-seeking, weapons assistance, cyberattacks, and deception.

verification.note: The supplier’s “loss of control” corresponds to the red lines on self-replication, self-improvement, and power-seeking; the phrase itself does not appear.

entries.name: Tsinghua AIR
entries.org: Institute for AI Industry Research (AIR), Tsinghua University
entries.description: Tsinghua University institute for industry-applied AI (“to fuel the industrial upgrade … with AI technologies”), organised into AI+IoT, AI+transportation, AI+healthcare, big-data intelligence, and robotics research.

verification.note: The site shows no AGI, agent, or AI-trajectory programme; the supplier’s reason is not supported.

entries.name: Tsinghua SuperBench
entries.org: Foundation Model Research Center, Tsinghua University
entries.description: Large-model capability leaderboard from Tsinghua’s Foundation Model Research Center and Zhongguancun Laboratory (since 2024), built on five native benchmarks and model judges such as CritiqueLLM; it publishes bimonthly reports and refreshes its question sets each cycle to avoid overfitting to static tests.

entries.name: Stanford AI Index
entries.description: Annual report and dataset (2026 edition current) tracking AI technical performance, R&D, investment, adoption, education, and policy; it argues that independent measurement matters more as developer disclosure declines.

entries.name: Stanford HAI
entries.description: Stanford institute for research, education, and policy on AI and data science; it publishes the AI Index, policy briefs, and research, and funds fellowships and grants.

entries.name: CSET Georgetown
entries.org: Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET), Georgetown University
entries.reason: Compute, talent, frontier AI, China, national security
entries.description: Policy research centre analysing the security implications of AI, advanced computing, and biotechnology, with research lines on AI inputs (talent, data, compute), national-security applications, assessment, competition, and supply chains, backed by roughly 60 analysis-ready datasets.

entries.name: NIST CAISI
entries.org: NIST Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI)
entries.description: US government centre within NIST that leads unclassified evaluations of AI capabilities posing national-security risks (cyber, biological, chemical), evaluates US and adversary systems, develops AI security measurement guidelines, and holds voluntary testing agreements with developers.

verification.note: Formerly the US AI Safety Institute (renamed June 2025).

entries.name: State of AI Safety in China
entries.description: Annual State of AI Safety in China reports (2023–2026) tracking domestic and international governance, technical safety research, expert views, and industry practice; the 2026 edition reports a shift from content control toward controlling agentic AI actions, with agent safety the most active area of Chinese frontier-safety research.

entries.name: Chinese Technical AI Safety Database
entries.reason: Maps China's frontier safety research ecosystem
entries.description: Explorer over a database of frontier-AI safety papers with substantial Chinese-institution authorship (April 2023 – April 2026), classified into alignment, robustness, monitoring, and systemic safety, with profiles of 28 Chinese research groups.

verification.note: A distinct page from #31 on the same site; its own title is “Chinese Technical AI Safety Paper Database”.

entries.name: Center for AI Safety
entries.description: Nonprofit working to reduce societal-scale AI risk through technical and conceptual research, benchmarks (including work on deception, manipulation, and defining AGI), a compute cluster and fellowships for safety researchers, and advocacy for safety standards.

entries.name: Redwood Research
entries.description: Nonprofit researching risks from AI systems that deliberately act against their developers; it introduced the AI control research area, published evidence that language models can fake alignment, and advises developers and governments on risks from misaligned agents.

entries.name: Redwood AI Control
entries.reason: Control of potentially adversarial superhuman AI
entries.description: Overview of AI control: ensuring an AI cannot cause harm even if egregiously misaligned, assessed by a model’s capability to subvert safety protocols (such as weaker trusted models monitoring stronger untrusted ones) rather than its inclination to. It collects the paper “AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion” and the BashBench, BashArena, and LinuxArena settings.

entries.name: Alignment Research Center
entries.description: Nonprofit working to align future machine-learning systems with human interests; its current research is theoretical — mechanistic explanations of network behaviour, aiming at algorithms that predict behaviour from the weights rather than by sampling, applied to out-of-distribution prediction and anomaly detection.

verification.note: The site speaks of “future machine learning systems”, not explicitly of systems surpassing humans.

entries.name: FAR.AI
entries.description: Research and field-building organisation working on alignment (e.g. deception detection), robustness (adversarial attacks on safety systems), and model evaluations (vulnerabilities, persuasion); it runs alignment workshops, a Berkeley co-working space, and a grant programme.

entries.name: GovAI Research
entries.org: Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
entries.description: Research index of GovAI: papers, technical reports, and policy briefs on frontier-AI regulation, technical governance, risk management, security, threat modelling, AI and biosecurity, and economics.
aliases: Centre for the Governance of AI

verification.note: The site states GovAI is a US 501(c)(3) with a UK subsidiary; the supplier’s “US/global” is recorded as US.

entries.name: Frontier Model Forum
entries.description: Industry nonprofit of frontier developers (Amazon, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI) that publishes issue briefs and technical reports on frontier capability assessments and safety frameworks, runs the AI Safety Fund, and operates information-sharing workstreams on biological, cyber, nuclear, and security risks.

entries.name: Peking University Institute for AI
entries.org: Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Peking University
entries.description: Peking University’s AI institute (founded 2019), organised into centres for general AI, AI with the humanities and social sciences (including AI safety and governance), AI+medicine, and AI+science; it also hosts a large-model research centre and a world-model joint laboratory.

verification.note: The “General AI Institute” the supplier names is a sub-institute of this institute.

entries.name: PKU Large Model Research Center
entries.org: Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Peking University
entries.description: Peking University centre coordinating research on language, vision, multimodal, and embodied large models and their engineering systems, working with BAAI to pool compute and data for foundation-model training; it also studies data processing and safety governance for large models.

verification.note: Profile page only; no outputs listed. The English name is a translation of 大模型研究中心.

entries.name: PKU Multi-Agent & Social Intelligence
entries.org: Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Peking University
entries.description: Peking University centre on multi-agent systems — control, communication, coordination, cooperation, and competition among agents — applied to a reinforcement-learning “large management model” for industrial decisions, social simulation for urban governance, and a civilisation simulator of great-power and world-system dynamics.

verification.note: Profile page only; no outputs listed.

entries.name: Z.ai / Zhipu Research
entries.description: Research index for the GLM model family — base, multimodal, reasoning, agentic, and code models — including the GLM-5 technical report (from “vibe coding” to agentic engineering), GLM-5.x releases aimed at long-horizon tasks, and a GLM-5.3 report on emergent cyber capabilities.

verification.note: Individual articles now redirect to z.ai.

entries.name: ByteDance Seed
entries.description: ByteDance’s Seed team (founded 2023), researching language, speech, vision, world models, AI infrastructure, and interaction toward general intelligence; it releases the Seed2 language and agent models, Seedream, Seedance, and audio models, and runs Seed Edge, a long-term programme on general intelligence.

entries.name: ByteDance Seed Research
entries.description: Blog and publications of ByteDance Seed across foundation models, vision, audio, and infrastructure; recent items include EdgeBench (reporting a log-sigmoid scaling pattern in how agents learn in real environments), the Seed2.0 model card, large-scale training systems, and long-horizon robotic manipulation.

verification.note: The full paper list is at /en/public_papers.

entries.name: MiniMax Research
entries.description: MiniMax’s research page and model line (M3 and M2.x language models, H3 video, speech, music), with posts on lightning- and hybrid-attention architectures for long context (MiniMax-01, MiniMax-M1) and M3’s 1M-token native multimodal context.

entries.name: MiniMax
entries.description: Chinese-language corporate site of MiniMax, which states the goal of achieving AGI and lists its self-developed multimodal models (M3, M2.7, M2.5, H3 video, Speech 2.8, Music 3.0) and products.

verification.note: Same company as #46; minimax.io is its English site.

entries.name: ARC Prize / ARC-AGI
entries.reason: Explicit measurement of progress toward AGI
entries.description: Nonprofit running the ARC-AGI benchmarks (ARC-AGI-1 to -3) and prize competitions on Kaggle for open-sourced solutions; it defines AGI as matching human learning efficiency, targets tasks easy for humans and hard for AI, and keeps a verified model leaderboard.

entries.name: ARC-AGI-3
entries.description: Interactive benchmark in which agents explore novel game environments, infer goals, and learn continuously; it measures skill-acquisition efficiency, long-horizon planning under sparse feedback, and adaptation, with public games, human leaderboards, replays, and an agent toolkit.

entries.name: Metaculus AI Forecasting
entries.description: Forecasting platform aggregating participants’ probabilistic predictions; its long-running AI questions include the dates of weakly general AI, general AI, and transformative AI and the interval from weak AGI to superintelligence, and it runs AI tournaments and FutureEval, a benchmark of AI forecasting ability.

verification.note: Verified from search results on metaculus.com; the site blocks automated loading.

entries.name: Metaculus AI Forecasting Benchmark 2026
entries.description: Spring 2026 season of the AI Forecasting Benchmark (now FutureEval): registered bots forecast real-world questions, a subset also goes to professional forecasters for a direct bots-versus-humans comparison, and Metaculus reports that the professionals have won every season so far.

verification.note: Renamed FutureEval (hub at metaculus.com/futureeval/). Verified from search results on metaculus.com; the site blocks automated loading.

entries.name: Artificial Analysis
entries.description: Independent benchmarking company measuring models, the inference providers that serve them, and the chips they run on; it publishes the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and compares speed, latency, and cost across language, image, video, and speech models.

entries.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
entries.description: Model comparison ranking language models on Intelligence Index v4.3.2 — a composite of ten independently run evaluations including Terminal-Bench, SciCode, and Humanity’s Last Exam — with output speed, latency, price, and context window for 673 models on the check date.

verification.note: Index version, components, and model count change over time.

entries.name: Stanford CRFM
entries.description: Stanford HAI centre studying how foundation models are built and deployed — data, systems, training, evaluation, transparency, and policy; its projects include HELM, the Foundation Model Transparency Index, Levanter, and Ecosystem Graphs.

entries.name: Foundation Model Transparency Index
entries.description: Annual index scoring foundation-model developers on 100 transparency indicators covering data, labour, and compute inputs, capabilities and risks, and downstream use; the December 2025 edition scored 13 companies with a mean of 41, 17 points below the previous year, and found training data still opaque.

entries.name: OpenCompass
entries.description: Open evaluation system for language and multimodal models, publishing CompassRank leaderboards, a pairwise-vote arena, and domain benchmarks such as MMBench and LawBench.

verification.note: Verified from search results on its own domain; the homepage renders client-side. Leaderboards are at rank.opencompass.org.cn.

entries.name: Shanghai AI Lab AI45 Safety Evaluation
entries.description: The laboratory’s large-model safety evaluation system, supporting regulatory filing evaluations and collecting its safety benchmarks and judge models (SALAD-Bench, MD-Judge, MM-SafetyBench, and others), jailbreak research, and watermarking and deepfake-detection work.

verification.note: Content-safety and jailbreak evaluation, not capability benchmarks. The laboratory’s frontier risk-management framework (SafeWork-F1) is at ai45.shlab.org.cn/research/.

entries.name: C-Eval
entries.description: Chinese evaluation suite of 13,948 multiple-choice questions across 52 disciplines and four difficulty levels, from junior-high to professional exams, with a public leaderboard measuring the Chinese-language knowledge and reasoning of foundation models.

verification.note: The site’s TLS certificate expired on 11 September 2025, so browsers warn; the maintained repository is github.com/hkust-nlp/ceval.

entries.name: ModelScope
entries.description: Open-source model hub with model and dataset repositories for language, speech, and multimodal models, hosted demo spaces, and an MCP community.

verification.note: Its operator (Alibaba, per community pages) was not confirmed from a primary page.

entries.name: SenseTime Research
entries.description: Research on native multimodal foundation models (SenseNova U1, spatial-intelligence and multimodal search-reasoning models, lightweight agent models) and embodied AI built on world models (the Kaiwu world model).

entries.name: StepFun Research
entries.description: Research hub with technical write-ups including Step3 (an open multimodal reasoning mixture-of-experts with 321B total and 38B active parameters, co-designed with its serving system to cut decoding cost), Step-Audio 2, NextStep-1, Open-Reasoner-Zero, and StepFun-Prover.

verification.note: Newer model write-ups (Step 3.5 and 3.7 Flash) are at static.stepfun.com/blog/.

entries.name: Zhejiang Lab
entries.description: Hangzhou research institution (founded 2017) organised around intelligent computing — brain-like computing and intelligent-computing platforms for scientific uses such as astronomy and drug discovery.

verification.note: The English homepage has no foundation-model or frontier-AI content; its internal links point to en.zhejianglab.com.

entries.name: CAS Institute of Automation
entries.org: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CASIA)
entries.description: Chinese Academy of Sciences institute for intelligent science and technology (founded 1956) whose programme centres on “autonomously evolving intelligence” through brain-inspired intelligence, multimodal cognition, and game-theoretic decision-making; it hosts the State Key Laboratory of Multimodal AI Systems and an AI ethics and governance centre.

verification.note: www.ia.cas.cn presents an invalid certificate; the same site loads at ia.cas.cn.

entries.name: CASIA English Research Portal
entries.org: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CASIA)
entries.description: English portal of CASIA listing its research centres, including the International Research Center for AI Ethics and Governance, the Research Center for Brain-inspired Intelligence, and the National Laboratory of Pattern Recognition.

verification.note: Same institute as #63. HTTPS presents an invalid certificate, so the working address is http; the newest listed events date from 2021–22. Verified from search results and a direct load.

entries.name: China Academy of Information and Communications Technology
entries.org: China Academy of Information and Communications Technology (CAICT)
entries.description: Research institute under China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology that describes itself as a government think tank; it publishes white papers, blue books, and indices on AI and computing power, including a 2026 AI safety governance blue book and China computing-power development indices.

verification.note: The site blocks automated clients; verified from search results on caict.ac.cn.

entries.name: China Computing Network
entries.org: China Computing Network (中国算力网); operator not named
entries.description: Industry portal for China’s computing-power sector: news and trend analysis on chips, data centres, networking, and AI infrastructure, and a marketplace for trading compute.

verification.note: Not the national China Computing NET (C²NET), which shares the Chinese name 中国算力网 and is run by Peng Cheng Laboratory (pcl.ac.cn); this site states no operator or government affiliation.

entries.name: China AI Computing Development Report
entries.description: The 2026 China AI Computing Power Development Assessment Report, which attributes rising compute demand to agent token consumption and forecasts China’s intelligent-computing capacity at 2,576.5 EFLOPS in 2026 and 10,524.3 EFLOPS in 2030, with global active agents rising from 79.4 million to 2.216 billion over the same period.

entries.name: OpenAI Research
entries.description: Research index of publications and releases on GPT-series language, multimodal, and audio models, framed by OpenAI’s stated aim of AGI that benefits humanity.

verification.note: Verified from search results on openai.com, which blocks automated loading. Alignment research is also published at alignment.openai.com.

entries.name: OpenAI Preparedness Framework
entries.description: Version 2 (April 2025) of OpenAI’s Preparedness Framework: High and Critical capability thresholds for Tracked Categories (biological and chemical, cybersecurity, AI self-improvement), Research Categories such as long-range autonomy, sandbagging, and autonomous replication, and Capabilities and Safeguards Reports that record evaluations and mitigations.

verification.note: No newer version found on openai.com; the later Frontier Governance Framework states that the Preparedness Framework remains its foundation. Verified from search results on openai.com.

entries.name: Anthropic Research
entries.description: Research index of Anthropic’s Alignment, Interpretability, Economics, Societal Impacts, and Frontier Red Team teams on model safety, internal mechanisms, and societal effects.

entries.name: Anthropic Institute
entries.description: Anthropic programme on the consequences of powerful AI, publishing three scenarios for the US economy through 2030 that vary capability and adoption pace, metrics on the pace of AI-led R&D and safety-compute allocation inside a frontier lab, and an analysis of futures under recursive self-improvement.

verification.note: The scenarios seen are economic; no separate scientific scenarios were found.

entries.name: Google DeepMind Research
entries.description: Research overview: agents and robotics (SIMA 2, Gemini Robotics), interactive world models (Genie 3), game-playing systems, and publications including frontier-model evaluations.

verification.note: Recorded as UK: Google DeepMind states its headquarters is in London (supplied as US).

entries.name: DeepMind Frontier Safety
entries.description: May 2024 introduction of the Frontier Safety Framework: Critical Capability Levels at which models could cause severe harm, early-warning evaluations to detect models approaching them, and security and deployment mitigations; the first version covered autonomy, biosecurity, cybersecurity, and ML R&D.

verification.note: The /discover/blog/ path redirects (HTTP 301) to /blog/. The current version is 3.1 (April 2026), listed at deepmind.google/frontier-safety/; version 3 added a harmful-manipulation level, misalignment risk assessment, and Tracked Capability Levels. Recorded as UK (supplied as US/UK).

entries.name: Meta AI Research
entries.description: Meta’s AI research page, now centred on the Muse models (Muse Spark multimodal reasoning, the open-weight Muse Glimmer, Muse Image), with safety reports under Meta’s Advanced AI Scaling Framework covering chemical, biological, cyber, and loss-of-control risks.

verification.note: No longer a general FAIR index, and Muse Spark is closed-weight. The page renders client-side; content confirmed from search results on ai.meta.com.

entries.name: Microsoft Research AI
entries.description: AI research-area hub aggregating projects, labs, and publications across vision, language, audio, and health, with recent work on agent evaluation, LLM reasoning, and the security of generated code.

entries.name: NVIDIA Research
entries.description: Research portal covering machine learning, 3D deep learning, vision, and robotics, with labs including Spatial Intelligence, Autonomous Vehicles, and Deep Imagination, linked to the Nemotron agentic models, Cosmos physical-AI models, and open research libraries.

verification.note: research.nvidia.com redirects (HTTP 301) here. No scaling or compute-trend research appears on the landing page.

entries.name: Allen Institute for AI
entries.description: Nonprofit institute that trains and releases fully open models — OLMo language models, Molmo multimodal models, Tülu post-training — with their data, code, weights, and evaluation frameworks, so the full training flow can be inspected.

entries.name: Berkeley CHAI
entries.description: UC Berkeley centre for the theory, practice, and policy of beneficial AI, which argues that optimising a fixed proxy for value is insufficient; it publishes on goal misgeneralisation, human-AI coordination, and offline reinforcement learning.

entries.name: Machine Intelligence Research Institute
entries.description: Organisation that credits its earlier work with helping found AI alignment and now argues that artificial superintelligence would by default cause human extinction; its technical governance team has published an example international agreement to prevent premature superintelligence, built on training-compute thresholds, AI-chip tracking, and research restrictions.

verification.note: miri.org is an unrelated personal site; MIRI’s own site is intelligence.org. Classed as governance because its current work centres on a superintelligence moratorium.

entries.name: Palisade Research
entries.description: Studies the capabilities and motivations of current AI agents to understand the risk of losing control to them, with experiments on shutdown resistance and specification gaming in reasoning models, autonomous hacking and self-replication, and cheap removal of safety fine-tuning from open-weight models.

entries.name: Apollo Research
entries.description: Researches scheming — AI that pursues its own goals while appearing aligned: how scheming emerges, methods to detect it, and pre-deployment scheming evaluations of frontier models for developers, plus governance work on loss of control and internal deployment.

verification.note: Recorded as UK: the organisation describes itself as London-based, with most staff in London or San Francisco; since 2026 it is a Delaware public-benefit corporation (supplied as US).

entries.name: RAND Artificial Intelligence
entries.description: RAND’s AI research hub: AI governance and making future systems safer, military applications, workforce displacement, and adversary use of AI, with recent reports on US strategy for artificial superintelligence and on managing risk on the road to advanced AI.

entries.name: CSIS Artificial Intelligence
entries.org: Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS)
entries.description: Hub for CSIS analysis of AI’s implications for warfare, US national security, and the global economy, drawing on the Wadhwani AI Center, Futures Lab, and technology programmes; recent items cover global AI governance, US federal AI spending, and AI-agent containment failures.

entries.name: CSIS AI & Future of Conflict
entries.description: Futures Lab project on how AI reshapes military operations, strategic decisions, and diplomacy, along three lines — AI, war and strategy; stress-testing AI systems for high-stakes use; and AI for conflict resolution — with congressional tabletop exercises and reports on AI and deterrence.

entries.name: CNAS Artificial Intelligence
entries.org: Center for a New American Security (CNAS)
entries.description: CNAS Technology and National Security page on AI: bottlenecks to AI progress (energy, compute infrastructure), governance frameworks, and AI partnerships abroad; it links the AI Security and Stability project on advanced-AI risk in cyber, biological, and nuclear domains, compute governance, and Chinese AI decision-making.

verification.note: The listed /topics/artificial-intelligence returns 404; this is the AI page linked from the CNAS homepage. The AGI and loss-of-control work (including #15) sits at cnas.org/ai-security.

entries.name: Carnegie Endowment — AI
entries.description: Carnegie Endowment AI research, oriented to anticipating international security challenges from AI over 2–5 and 5–10 year horizons, including a China AI Initiative on China’s AI ecosystem, governance, and US–China competition.

verification.note: The listed path redirects (HTTP 301) to /topics/ai, which renders client-side; content was read from the programme’s AI collection page.

entries.name: Brookings AI / Technology Innovation
entries.description: Brookings research and commentary on AI across its AI and Emerging Technology Initiative, Governance Studies, Economic Studies, and Foreign Policy programmes; recent items address access in AI evaluation, the economics of specialisation, and financing AI infrastructure.

verification.note: The listed path redirects (HTTP 301) from /topic/ to /topics/.

entries.name: Atlantic Council GeoTech Center
entries.description: Programme on the geopolitical and societal effects of emerging technology, publishing briefs on national AI strategies and running the GeoTech Commission on AI, whose June 2026 report sets out a roadmap for US AI leadership.

entries.name: Special Competitive Studies Project
entries.description: Nonprofit making recommendations for US competitiveness as AI reshapes national security and the economy, aimed at winning the “techno-economic competition by 2030”; it maintains a Tech Scorecard tracking US–China technology competition and publishes reports on AI in the military and intelligence.

entries.name: Institute for Progress
entries.reason: Compute, science, AI policy and future growth
entries.description: Think tank for accelerating scientific, technological, and industrial progress, with policy work on metascience, high-skilled immigration, biotechnology, and emerging technology, including how the US should prepare for automated AI R&D and a speed-for-security bargain for AI data centres.

verification.note: Could not be loaded (connection reset, HTTP 403). Search results show the root still titled as the lab’s site, but several ai.tencent.com/ailab pages are now indexed as Tencent Yuanbao pages; the lab’s current output could not be confirmed.

entries.name: Alibaba DAMO Academy
entries.description: Alibaba’s research institute for basic science and applied technology, which published annual Top 10 Technology Trends forecasts (editions to 2023 on the site) alongside research-area and lab pages and the Alibaba Innovative Research programme.

verification.note: No trends edition after 2023 was found. The homepage renders client-side; details confirmed from search results on the domain.

entries.name: Qwen
entries.description: Home of the Qwen model family and Qwen Chat, with research posts on releases such as Qwen3 (dense and mixture-of-experts open-weight models including Qwen3-235B-A22B), Qwen3-VL, Qwen3-Omni, and Qwen3.5; the team states that it aims at artificial general intelligence.

verification.note: The Alibaba affiliation appears in page metadata, not visible text. The homepage renders client-side; content confirmed from search results on qwen.ai.
Could not be loaded (connection reset, HTTP 403); search results show the site titled “website under maintenance” (网站维护中). No other official address was found.

entries.name: Huawei Noah's Ark Lab
entries.description: Huawei’s AI research lab; its model-architecture direction targets foundational structures and optimisation algorithms for moving “from AI to AGI”, alongside time-series, optimisation, perception, and physical-intelligence work, and recent items include ScienceFlow, a loop that lets agents advance research projects autonomously.

entries.name: 01.AI
entries.description: Beijing company (founded May 2023) now centred on enterprise AI — industry agents, the WorldWise enterprise LLM platform, and sovereign-model training — whose one named model is Yi-Lightning, a 100B-parameter mixture-of-experts.

verification.note: No foundation-model release after Yi-Lightning is shown.

entries.name: SenseTime
entries.description: Builder of the SenseNova native multimodal foundation models (unified understanding and generation with interleaved multimodal chain-of-thought) and the SenseCore compute infrastructure, with agent and vision products.

verification.note: The homepage does not mention world models; see #60 for SenseTime’s world-model research.

entries.name: Chinese Academy of Sciences IIE
entries.org: Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences
entries.description: Chinese Academy of Sciences institute for information-security research — cryptography, data security, network and system security, and information-system testing and evaluation — whose recent activity includes a 2026 workshop on large-model privacy protection.

verification.note: HTTPS presents a self-signed certificate, so the working address is http. Model-risk and governance content is limited.

entries.name: Chinese Association for Artificial Intelligence
entries.description: China’s national learned society for AI (founded 1981), publishing CAAI Artificial Intelligence Research and other journals and more than 40 discipline and development reports since 2015, and running conferences, including a 2026 conference on large models and embodied interaction.

verification.note: A professional society, classed with research institutes.

entries.name: National Information Center of China
entries.description: Public institution under China’s National Development and Reform Commission for macroeconomic monitoring and forecasting and medium- and long-term trend studies; its AI publications include an AI industry-application reference architecture (2024) and a 2026 study on AI talent cultivation.

verification.note: Its own English name is State Information Center; “National Information Center of China” is the supplier’s translation.
